title: Rivermark - Governance & Egress Lockdown Technical Sync
topics: egress control patterns and blocking risky endpoints
RBAC, SSO and least privilege for control plane
summary: Rivermark and Redwood went through a focused technical review of Rivermark's private deployment requirements: strict egress controls, proof of KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO expectations for audit trails, and RBAC/SSO mapping. Redwood proposed an egress proxy pattern with allowlists, host-based firewall + subnet segmentation, KMS-integration options (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM), and visibility hooks (audit streams to customer SIEM). Next steps: run a short benchmark in Rivermark's staging VPC, exchange SOC2 artifacts, and provide a draft ops-runbook for egress fail-open handling.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report and ISO mapping matrix (Maya) by 2026-11-09
Rivermark to provide staging VPC CIDR, list of internal SIEM endpoints, and KMS policy contact (Tom) by 2026-11-12
Schedule a 2-hour pilot runbook test in staging (Diego + Evan) w/in two weeks
action_items: Maya Chen: Send SOC2 + ISO docs and security deck link (due 2026-11-09)
Diego Alvarez: Draft egress proxy config example and firewall ruleset snippets (due 2026-11-11)
Tom Berg: Share staging VPC details and KMS admin contact (due 2026-11-12)
Priya Patel: Validate required audit events list and retention window (due 2026-11-13)
questions: Can Redwood's control plane be put behind our SAML SSO with enforced 2FA?
How does the KV cache behave during network partitions and what metadata is logged?
What's the expected token/credential lifecycle for short-lived node credentials?
Will Redwood push audit logs directly to our Splunk/Datadog forwarder or provide a pull endpoint?
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 16:00 - 16:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Artifacts referenced: redwood-security-deck-v3.pdf (link), egress-runbook-draft.xlsx (link), SOC2-report-redwood-2026.pdf (link)

-- 00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everybody thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. we'll do a quick agenda: governance, egress, kms, logs, then ops runbook and next steps.
-- 00:22 Anika Rao: Thanks, Maya. We're time boxed for an hour, our main ask is that we can meet SOC2 controls around network egress and verify KMS integration for customer-managed keys. We also need to know how audit trails map to our retention policies.
-- 00:38 Diego Alvarez: Great. Just to set expectations — Redwood private gives you a control plane that can sit in your VPC, and serving nodes run in customer subnet. For egress we normally recommend an egress proxy pattern plus firewall rules at the subnet level.
-- 01:05 Tom Berg: Quick Q — can we force all outbound to a single egress proxy that we control, and have Redwood never touch public internet?
-- 01:18 Diego Alvarez: Yes, that's the common pattern. You can route nodes' NAT through your egress proxy / gateway. If you want air-gapped, we can also support a pull model for model artifacts via an internal mirror. There are tradeoffs for model updates.
-- 01:42 Priya Patel: When you say "pull model" is that a manual sync or can it be automated inside an isolated subnet? We need audit trail on when artifacts are fetched.
-- 01:55 Leah Brooks: Pull can be automated. We have an agent that can run in your isolated network that fetches signed artifacts from a customer mirror or from Redwood over a whitelisted endpoint. All fetches are logged with timestamps and a signed checksum.
-- 02:12 Evan Mo: Are those logs pushed off-host or do we consume them via your control plane? We prefer to pull into our Splunk collector, not to rely on push.
-- 02:26 Diego Alvarez: We can do both. By default control-plane audit events are emitted to an S3-compatible bucket. We also support a forwarder pattern that can push to your Splunk/Datadog collector endpoint via HTTPS with mutual TLS. If you prefer pull, we'll give structured event files with sequence numbers you can fetch.
-- 03:03 Anika Rao: On encryption: we must have CMKs in our KMS and rotate keys every 90 days. Is that supported?
-- 03:16 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support customer-managed keys. Two integration modes: 1) Redwood uses your KMS/HSM to wrap model-encryption keys; Redwood never sees unwrapped keys. 2) For on-prem air-gapped installs, we can plug into your HSM via PKCS#11. Rotation we support via key aliasing and we can coordinate key rotation windows — but note you'll need to ensure nodes can touch the KMS endpoint during rotation.
-- 03:46 Tom Berg: That KMS endpoint is in our VPC, correct? We don't want any cross-cloud calls for key ops.
-- 03:53 Leah Brooks: Correct, KMS calls stay in your VPC when using customer-managed KMS. We can also provide a broker if you want to keep KMS calls on-prem.
-- 04:10 Priya Patel: About RBAC and SSO — can we enforce SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO to the control plane? Our security team requires SCIM for account lifecycle.
-- 04:23 Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. You can map groups to roles (admin, ops, reader). We also have token minting for short-lived node credentials that expire in configurable TTLs.
-- 04:45 Anika Rao: We need audit-level detail for node creds issuance — username, requesting principal, IP, and reason. Is that captured?
-- 04:56 Diego Alvarez: We capture issuance events with requester principal, request metadata, and the audit log includes the associated session id. IP capture depends on the network path — if we sit in your VPC we log the private source IP; if you route through a NAT we log the NAT IP. We'll include a mapping file.
-- 05:21 Tom Berg: About egress rules — we want to block all outbound except for a small allowlist of internal endpoints and the KMS endpoint. Is there a pattern you recommend for fallback when an allowlisted endpoint is temporarily down?
-- 05:36 Leah Brooks: We recommend a fail-closed posture for production: block everything by default. For availability we suggest implemented retries + local degraded model (quantized offline model) that can operate without egress for short windows. For model fetches, use a staging window and pre-warm caches.
-- 06:05 Priya Patel: How does the runtime behave if it can't reach the KMS during rotation? We can't have nodes crash and expose unencrypted cache.
-- 06:18 Diego Alvarez: Node key material is held encrypted; if KMS is unavailable and rotation occurs, the node will continue to use the currently wrapped key until rotation completes. We have conformance tests in the runbook that show no plaintext exposure. If you want higher assurance we can integrate an HSM-backed offline key escrow.
-- 06:44 Anika Rao: We need to ensure all relevant events go to our SIEM with sub-minute latency for incident forensics.
-- 06:55 Diego Alvarez: Sub-minute should be achievable with our push forwarder+mutual TLS. There may be a small batching window for cost reasons but we can push raw events for critical categories (auth, key ops, admin changes) immediately.
-- 07:22 Evan Mo: Are there built-in preventative controls to stop data exfil attempts, like content inspection or egress packet filters?
-- 07:33 Leah Brooks: We don't do deep content inspection on your blobs by default, but you can place an egress proxy with DLP in front of your gateway. We can also allowlist model endpoint hostnames and IPs, and firewall at the process level on the node.
-- 08:00 Tom Berg: Can Redwood provide hardened firewall snippets for iptables/nftables or Calico network policies for k8s?
-- 08:11 Diego Alvarez: Yes — we provide example Calico policies and host firewall templates tuned to block all non-KMS, non-SIEM outbound, and only allow the control plane endpoints. We'll send these as part of the runbook.
-- 08:31 Anika Rao: Regarding SOC2 artifacts — we'll need the auditor-facing report and the control mappings. Can you provide evidence for change control and incident response?
-- 08:45 Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll share the SOC2 report and a control matrix that maps Redwood controls to SOC2/ISO clauses. For incident response we can provide playbooks and a sample audit trail for a simulated incident.
-- 09:05 Priya Patel: Data residency — we need to ensure no data leaves our VPC for certain datasets. How do you support per-tenant routing and residency flags?
-- 09:18 Diego Alvarez: You can pin tenant workloads to dedicated subnets and dedicate reserved nodes in those subnets. The control plane will only reference metadata; actual payloads (inputs/outputs) stay in your network. For hosted logs we support storing audit artifacts into your S3 bucket in-region.
-- 09:46 Tom Berg: Ok let's talk ops runbook steps for a failover: if egress proxy is down how do we triage with minimal downtime?
-- 09:56 Leah Brooks: We'll provide a runbook with a triage checklist: 1) Switch DNS to secondary egress collector (if you use two), 2) promote pre-warmed model cache, 3) enable degraded-mode routing. We'll also include circuit breaker thresholds and monitoring queries.
-- 10:25 Anika Rao: For compliance, will your logs maintain immutable retention? We need WORM-like properties for some evidence windows.
-- 10:34 Diego Alvarez: We can write audit artifacts to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled or to a write-once ledger for the long retention window. We'll document the configuration needed.
-- 11:00 Tom Berg: Can we run a short benchmark in staging to validate egress behavior and KMS latency? We'd like to measure tail latency during rotation.
-- 11:12 Maya Chen: Yes. Proposed pilot: a two-week staging test where we exercise key rotation, simulated egress failures, and throughput at production QPS. Diego and Evan to coordinate.
-- 11:28 Evan Mo: We'll want the script and the list of test cases. Also, please include expected observability metrics and traces so we can map into our dashboards.
-- 11:42 Diego Alvarez: We'll hand over a benchmark harness plus dashboards. We'll also provide sample Prometheus exporters and spans for tracing.
-- 12:05 Anika Rao: A couple of nitty gritty items — SAML attribute mapping for groups, SCIM delta behavior on deprovision, and how service accounts are rotated.
-- 12:20 Leah Brooks: SCIM supports delta syncs; deprovision triggers immediate session invalidation. Service accounts are rotated via short-lived tokens and an automated rotation job. We'll give examples.
-- 12:39 Tom Berg: Any gotchas with private deploy on our VMware-based clusters vs cloud native?
-- 12:49 Diego Alvarez: The main gap is networking primitives — we rely on overlay networking and host firewall hooks. On VMware you may need a lightweight agent for host-level controls. We documented the agent footprint in the deck.
-- 13:08 Anika Rao: Good. I want to call out legal: we'll need an explicit clause in the contract for data not leaving region X and for auditors to access logs.
-- 13:21 Maya Chen: Understood. I'll loop legal and get a template addendum.
-- 13:35 Evan Mo: Last item, do you support rotating TLS certs for node-to-control-plane connections via our internal CA?
-- 13:45 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support mutual TLS with customer CA rotation. Nodes accept cert bundles from your CA and we can automate rotation through the node agent.
-- 14:00 Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps and owners (see action items). We'll aim to get SOC2/ISO artifacts over by Monday. Any final Qs?
-- 14:15 Anika Rao: No further questions. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end.
